text: A standing privileged account holds elevated rights all the time, whether anyone is actively using that privilege right now or not. That's a real, significant risk, not a theoretical one — the account is a maximum-value target the instant it's compromised, with no further escalation required.

Phishing an ordinary user gets an attacker a foothold. Phishing a standing domain admin gets them the whole environment, immediately, with no further escalation required. And most of an admin's actual working day doesn't require admin rights at all, so that exposure sits there, continuously, with no operational benefit most of the time.

Privileged access management exists to reduce that exposure, starting with credential vaulting: privileged passwords live in an encrypted vault instead of being memorized by an administrator or shared across a team in a spreadsheet. An admin checks a credential out when they need it, under a logged, individually-attributable event, and the vault often rotates the password afterward so it can't be reused outside that process.

Vaulting controls who can obtain a privileged credential, but not what happens once they use it. Session recording closes that gap by capturing the commands and screen activity of the privileged session itself. That turns an incident investigation into an exact record instead of a guess, and makes routine privileged activity auditable even when nothing went wrong.

This is real, established tooling, not an abstract model. CyberArk is one of the longest-standing dedicated PAM platforms, built around vaulting, session recording, and privileged workflow automation across on-prem and cloud systems. Azure PIM, built into Microsoft Entra ID, is the cloud-native version focused specifically on role-based privileged access in Azure and Microsoft 365.

Azure PIM is also the mechanism behind just-in-time role activation — granting that privileged role only for the window it's actually needed, then automatically taking it back. That's exactly where Lesson 12 picks up next.
